context.guidance: Require authentication on every route that returns Personal Data, and check on each request that the authenticated Data Principal owns the record or holds a role authorised for it. Do not let an identifier supplied in the path or body decide ownership. Apply the check to every method on the route, because Rule 6(1)(b) requires access to the resources holding Personal Data to be controlled.

value.fix: Stop building the write destination from client-supplied names, and stop writing personal-data PDFs into the 'ftp/' directory, which may be publicly reachable. (1) Generate the filename server-side, for example crypto.randomUUID() + '.pdf'. If pdfFile must be kept, reduce it with path.basename() and reject anything that is not a plain alphanumeric name ending in .pdf. Resolve the final path with path.resolve() and confirm it starts with the intended private storage root before calling fs.createWriteStream. (2) Store these PDFs in a private directory outside any FTP or static-file root, and serve them only through an authenticated route. (3) On every route that creates, reads, or serves these PDFs, for all HTTP methods, require authentication. Then check that the authenticated Data Principal owns the record or holds a role authorised for it. Take the user identity from the session and the owner from the stored record, never from an ID in the path or body. (4) Attach error handlers to the write stream and do not expose the file until the write has finished. Verify with tests that a traversal name such as '../x.pdf' is rejected and that a request from a non-owner to the PDF route returns 403 and no file content.
